name: java-guide

Apply to Java files (`.java`), `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, or Java-related requests. Java 17+, Spring Boot, Maven/Gradle, enterprise applications.

**Standards**
- Prefer records, `final` fields, unmodifiable collections, composition, and standard-library APIs.
- Validate inputs at boundaries; use `Objects.requireNonNull`. Use explicit types; avoid raw types and unchecked casts.
- Use Java 17+ (LTS) with preview features disabled in production
- Use Maven (`pom.xml`) or Gradle (`build.gradle.kts`); pin dependency versions (no dynamic versions).
- Follow [Google Java Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html). Classes: `PascalCase`; methods/fields: `camelCase`; constants: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`; packages: lowercase, e.g. `com.company.project.module`.
- One top-level class per file, named for the file. Use `var` only when the type is obvious.
- No wildcard imports (`import java.util.*` is forbidden)
- Prefer records for immutable data carriers; use sealed types for restricted hierarchies and exhaustive pattern-matching switches. Validate records with compact constructors.
- Use streams for transformations, not side effects. Never call `Optional.get()` -- use `orElseThrow()`, `orElse()`, `map()`, `flatMap()`. Do not use `Optional` as a method parameter or field type (only as a return type). Avoid parallel streams unless measured faster; prefer `toList()` over `collect(Collectors.toList())`.
- Always use try-with-resources for `AutoCloseable` types. Never rely on `finalize()` (deprecated and unreliable). Close resources in reverse acquisition order.
- Prefer immutable factories/copies such as `List.of`, `Map.ofEntries`, and `List.copyOf`.

**Project/testing**
Use bounded-context packages; keep `resources/` flat and migrations in `db/migration/`. Suggested source root: `java/com/company/project/` (`Application.java`, `config/`, `controller/`, `service/`, `repository/`, `model/`, `dto/`, `exception/`); migrations: `db/migration/`; tests mirror source at `test/java/com/company/project/` and `src/test/java`; build output `target/` is gitignored.
Name tests `ClassNameTest`; use descriptive behavior-focused tests, parameterized tests for related cases, AssertJ, and mocks where appropriate. Coverage targets: >80% business logic, >60% overall.

**Commands**
mvn clean install              # Build and install locally
mvn test                       # Run all tests
mvn verify                     # Run tests + integration tests
mvn dependency:tree            # Show dependency tree
mvn dependency:analyze         # Find unused/undeclared deps
mvn spotbugs:check             # Static analysis
mvn checkstyle:check           # Style check
./gradlew build                # Full build with tests
./gradlew test                 # Run unit tests
./gradlew check                # Run all verification tasks
./gradlew dependencies         # Show dependency tree
./gradlew jacocoTestReport     # Generate coverage report
mvn org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:check
gradle dependencies

See `references/patterns.md` for Spring, streams, Optional, and builders. Also consult [Effective Java](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/effective-java/9780134686097/), [Java Records (JEP 395)](https://openjdk.org/jeps/395), [Sealed Classes (JEP 409)](https://openjdk.org/jeps/409), [Pattern Matching for switch (JEP 441)](https://openjdk.org/jeps/441), [JUnit 5](https://junit.org/junit5/docs/current/user-guide/), [AssertJ](https://assertj.github.io/doc/), [SpotBugs](https://spotbugs.github.io/), and [Checkstyle](https://checkstyle.org/).
